subject: Recap & next steps — regional compliance constraints and deployment options
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Sokolov <maria.sokolov@finserv-eu.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Recap & next steps — regional compliance constraints and deployment options

Hi Maria — thanks again for the time this morning. Short recap from our side and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard
- Residency constraint: all customer PII and transaction logs must remain in the EU (no cross-border replication to APAC or US).
- Latency targets: 95th percentile < 120ms for user-facing inference from EU locations.
- Throughput: ~150 QPS average, 600 QPS peak (burstable during end-of-day reporting).
- Security: KMS integration required, customer-managed keys preferred; SOC 2 and penetration-testing evidence needed for procurement.

Deployment options we discussed (high level)
- Hosted (EU-only): Redwood-hosted API with data pinned to EU regions; simple and fastest to get going, can offer EU-only tenancy and regionally-scoped storage.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in an EU region — good for predictable throughput and SLOs, data stays in-region.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Private control plane + customer VPC or on-prem package for fully isolated networks and customer-controlled KMS. Best for strict regulatory controls.

Questions / unknowns from our side
- Do you need an on-prem binary (air-gapped) or is a VPC-hosted private deployment sufficient?
- Which EU country/region do you prefer for residency (e.g., eu-west-1 vs eu-central-1)?
- Any contractual routing requirements (e.g., must fail to a secondary EU region rather than outside EU)?

Immediate next steps
1) Please send the filled security questionnaire (I attached the common form) — that will let our security team pre-validate controls.
2) If you can confirm preferred EU region and whether VPC vs on-prem is required, we’ll produce a short options matrix with 1) estimated monthly costs, 2) lead time, and 3) KMS/integration notes.
3) Proposed tech deep-dive: Tue/Thu next week — 45 minutes to walk infra, SLA, and key exchange details.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf (high level hosting vs private), fs-security-questionnaire.xlsx (blank)

Thanks — I’ll loop in Grace from Solutions to prepare the options matrix once you confirm region/VPC requirement.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0113

——

From: Maria Sokolov <maria.sokolov@finserv-eu.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: IT Security <sec@finserv-eu.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — regional compliance constraints and deployment options

Thanks, Logan — great recap. A few clarifications from compliance and procurement: 

- Residency: must be EU data centers only; replication outside EU is not permitted. 
- Failover: we require a secondary EU region for HA (e.g., primary eu-central-1 with failover to eu-west-1). No automatic failover to APAC/US.
- Deployment preference: leaning toward Private VPC (customer-managed network) so we can attach our corporate FW and logging. On-premises air-gapped is possible but adds months to timeline; prefer to avoid unless absolutely necessary.
- KMS: we require customer-controlled keys (bring-your-own-key) with audit logs.
- Evidence: please provide SOC 2 Type II report and results of most recent external penetration test; procurement will need these to start the PO.

Procurement timeline: we are targeting an internal decision window of 4–6 weeks. I attached our security questionnaire filled with initial answers (see attached).

Next steps from our side: we can book the tech deep-dive for Thu 10:00 AM CET — I will invite the security engineer (cc’d) to that meeting.

Cheers,
Maria
Head of Cloud Risk & Compliance | FinServ EU
Maria.Sokolov@finserv-eu.com

Attachment: fs-security-questionnaire.xlsx (partially completed)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Recap & next steps — regional compliance constraints and deployment options

Logan — quick internal note. Good capture of the ask. A few operational points before we reply publicly: 

- Private VPC in EU: product supports Private control plane with regional data placement. We need SRE to confirm capacity for 600 QPS peak in a single region; if they cannot guarantee that we should recommend Dedicated capacity pinned to eu-central-1.
- Failover policy: we can do secondary EU region only; we need to document explicit routing policy in the SOW to prevent cross-region failover outside EU.
- KMS: BYOK supported via customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) for Private and Dedicated. Hosted (shared tenancy) supports envelope encryption but not BYOK today — call that out.
- Evidence: attach SOC2 Type II and red-team summary (redwood-soc2-type2.pdf will be included). Procurement should see a short checklist of what we can commit (SLA, data residency, KMS options).

I’ll draft the options matrix and estimate (cost + lead time). Logan, can you confirm whether FinServ needs a temporary cross-region read-replica during data migration? That changes the migration playbook.

—Grace
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Sokolov <maria.sokolov@finserv-eu.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — regional compliance constraints and deployment options

Maria — thanks for the clear answers and for uploading the questionnaire. Short answers to your asks plus proposed immediate steps: 

Residency & failover
- We can commit to EU-only data residency. Replication and failover will be restricted to EU regions only and we will include that language in the SOW. Primary/secondary pairings (eu-central-1 <-> eu-west-1) are supported.

Deployment recommendation based on current constraints
- Private VPC (preferred): supports BYOK, VPC peering, corporate FW attachment, and audit logs. Estimated lead time: 6–8 weeks (includes networking and KMS onboarding).
- Dedicated capacity (alternative): reserved GPU pools in eu-central-1 with strict in-region data placement. Faster lead time (2–3 weeks) and lower operational lift than on-prem, but BYOK is supported via customer-managed KMS in Dedicated config.
- Hosted (not recommended given BYOK requirement): we can offer EU-only hosting, but BYOK for shared-hosting is not available today.

Documentation and evidence
- Attached: redwood-soc2-type2.pdf (SOC 2 Type II) and redwood-deployment-options.pdf.
- I’ve also created a short checklist for procurement and SRE to sign off on (link to Drive in related links).

Next steps
1) Confirm Thu 10:00 AM CET for the technical deep-dive.
2) We’ll follow up with a short options matrix (cost / lead-time / KMS notes) by EOD Wed. Grace will own the matrix.
3) If you plan any data migration that requires a temporary cross-region replica during cutover, please flag it now — we’ll need to scope that separately.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0113

Attachments: redwood-soc2-type2.pdf, redwood-deployment-options.pdf
